name: Reduce motion, contrast, color inversion and bold text
plain: Reads display accessibility toggles with no prompt.
meaning: A combination of 5 to 8 toggles gives a small fingerprint and hints at motion sensitivity or vision needs.

limits.headline: Can see whether Reduce Motion, high contrast, inversion or bold text is on
limits.user_action: Nothing. It happens when the app draws its screens
can: Check if Reduce Motion is on and skip heavy animations
Check for color inversion, bold text and similar toggles
Adjust screens to match your accessibility settings
cannot: See which assistive app you use
Warn you; there is no prompt
limits.reach_label: A handful of on or off settings
limits.differs: iPhone gives a yes or no for each toggle. Android also shows the animation scale from 0 to 10.

story.what_it_is: An app can see if you turned on Reduce Motion, high contrast, inverted colors or bold text.

marketing.name: Display accessibility
marketing.pitch: Apple offers settings for text size, contrast and motion so the phone fits how you see and move.

marketing.name: Android accessibility
marketing.pitch: Android offers settings like color correction, high contrast text and removing animations.

story.for_you: You turn on a setting and apps respond, with fewer swoops and easier to read text. You never see apps read it. It may also tell an app that you have trouble with motion or vision.
story.for_makers: Makers use these flags to calm animations, raise contrast and be inclusive. Together they also form a small fingerprint, and a combination of several toggles can imply a health or disability condition.

use_cases.example: A game cuts screen shake and flashes when Reduce Motion is on.
A social feed skips auto playing video and zoom effects for people who get dizzy.
A video app raises caption contrast when high contrast text is on.
An AR app tones down moving effects for people who feel sick with motion.
A store app switches to simpler transitions when Reduce Motion is on.
A tracker records the toggles as a profile, which can reveal a possible disability.

story.android_note: Android apps read many of these from system settings with no prompt.
story.ios_note: iPhone apps get a notification when each toggle changes and can read them with no prompt.
